 Judgment

Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-KL-7823 asserting that on 23.03.2023 at about 5.30 p.m. when petitioner along with Chiranjivi are walking on the left side of the road near Bishop Cotton School, St.Marks road, Bengaluru, rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-KL-7823 , rode the same negligently, dashed the same to the petitioner , thereby caused accident , caused injuries to the petitioner.

2. Petitioner took treatment at HOSMAT hospital , Bengaluru by spending Rs.3,00,000/-, as on the date of accident petitioner being aged 35 years, used to earn Rs.46,137/p.m. by working as Senior Engineer at Axiscades Technologies Limited, Bengaluru.
3. Regarding accident Cubbon Park Traffic police registered crime No.32/2023 against the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-KL-7823 .
4. Inspite of the service of the notice respondent No.1 remained absent.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through his Advocate,
filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner .
6.

On the basis of the pleadings on 09.02.2024 , this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 23.03.2023 at about 05.30 p.m. near Bishop Cotton School, St.Mark's Road, Bengaluru, he met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-03-KL-7823 as alleged?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
7. On 02.04.2024, 10.07.2024 petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 14 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14.

On 31.07.2024, petitioner produced the evidence of Dr.Rajesh M.B. and Smt. Shanthamma S.
as PW2 and 3 and produced 7 documents at Ex.P.15 to P.21.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

9. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues and additional issue are as under:

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 23.03.2023 at about 5.30 p.m. when walking along with Chiranjivi on the left side of the road St.Marks road, near Bishop Cotton School,
Bengaluru, rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-KL-7823 , rode the same negligently, dashed the same to the petitioner , thereby caused accident , caused injuries to the petitioner.
11.
In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
12. In the cross-examination petitioner stated that prior to the accident he never saw the appearance of the motorcycle .
Petitioner denied the suggestion that in the police records nothing has been mentioned about whether he was walking on the road or standing on the footpath during accident.
Petitioner stated that the report submitted by the police to the effect that when he was crossing the road at Anil Kumble circle , the accident taken place is wrong.
Petitioner stated that in the place where accident taken place there are no zebra mark.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that when he made efforts to cross the road negligently without watching the appearance of the vehicle the accident taken place.
13. In the evidence PW2 Dr.Rajesh M.B. stated nothing regarding reason and mode of accident.

14. In the evidence affidavit PW3 Shanthamma, MRD at HOSMAT hospital produced inpatient records, outpatient record, MLC report and police intimation at Ex.P.18 to P.21.
15.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.32/2023 registered by Cubbon Park traffic police against respondent No.1 rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-KL-7823 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC , 184 of IMV Act on the basis of the complaint presented by Chiranjeevi Aurrav Simha .

Ex.P.2 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Cubbon Park Traffic police in crime No.32/2023 against respondent No.1 Jai Shankar for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,338 of IPC Section 134(B) and 184 of IMV Act .
Ex.P.3 is the copy of the spot mahazar recorded on 24.03.2023.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of the wound certificate in which reason for the injuries is noted as hit by two wheeler 23.03.2023 at 5.00 p.m.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of the sketch of place of accident.
16. In this case respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason and mode of accident.
In this case respondent No.1 owner/rider of the motorcycle remained absent.
Hence, I have concluded that on 23.03.2023 at about 5.30 p.m. when petitioner along with Chiranjivi are walking on the left side of the road near Sandesh.

3

Bishop Cotton School, St.Marks road, Bengaluru, respondent No.1 Jai Shankar negligently rode the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-KL-7823 , dashed the same to the petitioner , thereby caused accident , caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered left leg bone 1/3rd fracture , took treatment at HOSMAT hospital , Bengaluru underwent multiple surgeries by spending approximately Rs.3,00,000/- and as on the date of accident being aged about 35 years used to earn Rs.46,137/-p.m. by working as Senior Engineer at Axiscades Technologies Limited,
Bengaluru.
18. In the written statement, respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

19. In the cross-examination, petitioner admitted non-production of documents regarding loss of income due to the accident and in Axiscades Technologies Limited, Bengaluru there are facility of medical reimbursement .
Petitioner has stated about spending of Rs.2,00,000/- for treatment and reimbursement made by the company worth of Rs.1,50,000/-.

Petitioner denied the suggestion that the company reimbursed the entire medical bills, however fabricated 33 medical bills marked at Ex.P.9.
20.

In the evidence affidavit PW2 Dr. Rajesh M.B. stated that on 17.07.2024 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that the petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 38% to left lower limb and he needs another surgery to get removal of implant at the cost of Rs.60,000/-
and produced the recent x-ray .
Clinical assessment proforma along with calculation sheet marked at Ex.P.15 and P.16.

In the cross-examination PW2 stated that he never treated the petitioner,
however verified the wound certificate and discharge summary.
PW2 stated that even after removal of implant quantum of the physical disability will not decrease.
In the evidence PW3 stated nothing regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

21. Wound certificate, discharge summary, prescriptions, medical bills , case files, x-ray shows that in the accident petitioner suffered left leg both bone fracture , took treatment at HOSMAT hospital as an inpatient from 23.03.2023 to 26.03.2023 by spending approximately Rs.39,300/- excluding the money reimbursed by the company.
In the xerox copy of the aadhar card date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 04.10.1987.

Salary slip marked at Ex.P.12 shows that during January 2023 and February 2023 petitioner by working as Senior Engineer at Axiscades Technologies Limited,
Bengaluru earned gross salary of Rs. 48,137/p.m. i.e., Rs.21,000/- basic, Rs.10,500/-, Rs.2,000/-
and Rs.14,637/- towards allowances.
22.

As referred above, in the evidence PW2 Dr.Rajesh M.B. submitted that he never treated the petitioner and in this case petitioner has not produced any type of evidence to show either decrease in the salary or loss of salary subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.
Hence, I have inferred that the oral evidence of PW2 Dr.Rajesh M.B. is not sufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income.

4 23.

Hence, I award Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.39,300/- towards treatment charges, Rs.10,000/- towards attendant , conveyance, nourishment charges, Rs.1,89,000/-
(Rs.31,500x6) towards loss of income during treatment period, Rs.75,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness.
24.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.4,13,300/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
25. In the written statement , respondent No.2 insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-KL-7823 as on the date of accident .
In this case there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident respondent No.1 violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-KL- 7823 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.
The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.4,13,300/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-03-KL-7823 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 10th day of October, 2024)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
